item.title: No BNP meeting held at Secretariat, say its leaders
item.description:
BNP leaders on Thursday denied that the party held a meeting at the Secretariat on the nomination of its candidate for the presidential election, rejecting criticism from opposition Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami.
“There was no meeting today. Since Tarique Rahman is the prime minister and our party chairman, we had entrusted him with the responsibility of choosing the candidate. He called us and informed us of the decision. There was no meeting there,” BNP Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy said.
He was speaking to reporters after submitting the nomination paper for BNP’s presidential candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to the Election Commission in the Nirbachan Bhaban.
The BNP leader was responding to a question about Jamaat's criticism over the announcement of Mirza Fakhrul as the BNP's presidential candidate following what was described as a party “meeting” at the Secretariat.
A BNP delegation, led by its Standing Committee member Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, submitted the nomination paper to Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, who is serving as the returning officer of the presidential election, at 2:24pm.
In the nomination paper, Moyeen Khan proposed Mirza Fakhrul as a presidential candidate while Gayeshwar Chandra seconded his candidacy.
Responding to the criticism, Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni, also a delegation member, reiterated that there was no meeting at the Secretariat in this regard.
“What took place at the Secretariat today was not a meeting. We held discussions there. Discussions can take place anywhere in Bangladesh,” he said, adding that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was nominated and elected from a party.
The chief whip said the decision on the presidential candidate had already been taken and Tarique Rahman just announced it now.
PM’s adviser and BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi also claimed that it was not a meeting of the BNP Standing Committee as it had earlier authorised Tarique Rahman to select the party’s presidential candidate.
Earlier in the morning, Jamaat Assistant Secretary General and coordinator of the 11-party alliance AHM Hamidur Rahman Azad questioned the holding of a BNP meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office in the Secretariat to select its candidate for the presidential election.
“The Secretariat is an executive place. A top-level political meeting has been held there! We are not aware of any such precedent. Yet they are doing it. So, how do they view democracy?” he told reporters after submitting the nomination paper for their alliance’s presidential candidate Col (retd) Oli Ahmad to the CEC.
During the briefing, Gayeshwar Chandra welcomed the 11-party alliance’s participation in the presidential election slated for August 20.
About the participation of both BNP and Jamaat-led opposition camps in the presidential election, Moni said: “The beauty of democracy is that we are contesting and being elected.”
Noting that this Parliament was formed through a neutral election after 17 years of movement, he said BNP Tarique Rahman is working to fulfil the expectations of the people.
The delegation members include Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee, whips of Parliament Miah Nuruddin Ahmed Apu, GK Gouse, ABM Ashraf Uddin (Nizan), Rakibul Islam and Akhtaruzzaman Miah, BNP joint secretaries general Habib Un-Nabi Khan Sohel and Abdus Salam Azad.

item.title: Parwar blames govt for power, gas crisis
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar has blamed the government’s alleged mismanagement, corruption and prisonization for the ongoing electricity and gas crisis.
In a statement sent to the media on Thursday, he said the country had been facing a severe power and gas crisis in recent days, with widening shortages increasing public suffering.
According to figures cited in the statement, load shedding reached 3,671MW on August 9, 3,757MW on August 10, 3,465MW on August 11 and 3,382MW on August 12.
Parwar said the figures indicated an average power shortfall of around 3,500MW in recent days, affecting both households and industries.
He also said that against a demand for 3.8 billion cubic feet of gas on August 12, supply stood at 2.03 billion cubic feet.
“Due to the government’s mismanagement, inefficiency, shortsightedness, widespread corruption and prisonization in various institutions, the electricity and gas crisis has reached an extreme level,” he said.
Parwar expressed concern over disruptions to people’s daily lives and condemned what he described as the government’s failure to address the crisis.
He said public anger was growing as the energy crisis worsened.
According to Parwar, the Bangladesh Rural Electrification Association has sent a letter to police headquarters seeking increased security at 80 rural electricity cooperatives across the country.
He said the move reflected the government’s failure to properly manage the electricity sector.
Citing media reports, Parwar said Nilphamari was receiving 45-55MW against a demand of 80MW, while Kushtia was receiving 85-95MW against a demand of 155MW.
He said similar shortages were being reported across the country, prompting electricity officials to seek additional security measures.
Parwar said the crisis had emerged because the government had failed to take long-term decisions on electricity management.
Industrial production was being disrupted, while power and gas shortages were making it difficult for people to carry out routine household activities, including cooking, he said.
Students were also facing disruptions to their studies, he added.
“Above all, people’s lives have become unbearable. In this situation, the government’s failure to take any effective initiative to resolve the crisis is an indication of its irresponsibility towards the people,” he said.
Parwar also expressed concern that the government could deepen the crisis by providing renewed benefits to old oligarchs in the name of privatizing the energy sector.
He called for increased gas supply, an end to industrial gas theft, measures to reduce leakages and system losses, easier import of energy-related equipment and technology, steps to prevent oil smuggling, and arrangements to import crude oil through government or private initiatives.
He also called for effective measures to improve the skills of those involved in electricity generation and distribution.
Parwar said foreign partners with expertise in onshore reservoir management and access to new technologies should be brought in to explore domestic gas reserves.
He also called for new exploration and development wells to be drilled to ensure the country’s energy security.
The Jamaat leader said the government would have to take responsibility for any deterioration in the situation if it failed to take necessary measures to meet people’s basic and daily needs.

item.title: Singapore interested in Bangladesh’s Bay Terminal project
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Thursday said Singapore has long had a proposal for a Bay Terminal at Chittagong Port, which came up for discussion during her recent visit to the country.
"You know that the Singapore government has had a proposal for a Bay Terminal at our Chittagong Port for a long time. They have talked about that," she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Shama Obaed said they also visited one of the projects where they have a waste-to-energy, and they have shown how they produce energy by managing waste.
During her first official visit to Singapore, the state minister met Singapore’s Foreign Affairs Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan and its State Minister for Foreign Affairs Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim separately and discussed issues of mutual interest.
She also visited the Port of Singapore Authority (PSA), where she met Regional CEO, Middle East, South Asia, Africa and Türkiye, PSA Vincent Ng, and senior officials.
The state minister was briefed on PSA’s global operations and its use of automation and advanced technologies to develop efficient, sustainable and smart ports.
Vincent Ng expressed PSA’s interest in participating in the Bay Terminal project in Bangladesh, noting its potential to significantly enhance Chittagong Port and Bangladesh’s trade and connectivity, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The state minister welcomed PSA’s interest and expressed hope for enhanced cooperation in port development, logistics, technology transfer and capacity building, in line with Bangladesh’s priorities of industrialisation, infrastructure development and connectivity.
"We discussed ways to deepen cooperation, including expanding trade and strengthening our energy partnership. We are also making good progress on a bilateral Free Trade Agreement, which will create more opportunities for businesses in both countries," said the Foreign Minister of Singapore.
He said Singapore and Bangladesh share a longstanding partnership and close people-to-people ties.
Bangladesh and Singapore on Tuesday expressed hope for the early conclusion of the Bangladesh-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and emphasised stronger business-to-business engagement.
The two countries also exchanged views on energy security, including risks to energy supplies, shipping and global supply chains, as well as climate change, water security, and illegal and irregular migration.

item.title: Hasan takes 6-55 as Bangladesh claim opening day of Australia Test
item.description:
Hasan Mahmud took a career-best 6-55 as Bangladesh bundled Australia out for 198 to take the honours on the opening day of the first Test in Darwin on Thursday.
Mominul Haque was on 35 with Tanzid Hasan alongside him on 32 as the visitors made a superb start to a Test match most people expected them to lose inside three days.
Earlier, Hasan led an impressive display by the visitors' seamers as Australia slumped to their lowest Test score against Bangladesh, their previous worst being 217 in Mirpur in 2017.
The 26-year-old was the pick of the attack, but he was ably supported by fellow quicks Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain, who took two wickets apiece.
"I was just trying to bowl line and length, trust the process and follow what the captain was saying," Hasan said.
"(Taskin and Ebadot) were trying their best and they did very well also."
Steve Smith was the only Australian to offer any resistance, scoring 71, while the rest of the batsmen looked out of sorts against the disciplined attack.
"We haven't played a Test match for a while and it can take some time to get into it," Smith said.
"It wasn't easy. The ball was doing stuff and you have to be patient.
"Perhaps we got dragged into a few we didn't need to, but that's the pressure."
After skipper Pat Cummins chose to bat on a perfect Darwin day, a full-strength Australia were expected to dominate a Bangladesh side who were well beaten by a Cricket Australia XI in their only warm-up match.
Hasan made the initial breakthrough in the 12th over with the score on 45.
Jake Weatherald, on 23, had a huge swipe at a ball outside off stump and only managed a thick edge to wicketkeeper Litton Das.
Hasan struck again soon after, fellow opener Travis Head chopping on for 22 to leave Australia 52-2.
Bangladesh then saw a huge opportunity go begging when Smith, on two, edged Ebadot to third slip where Tanzid Hasan spilled the chance.
Smith had a second escape next over when he got a thick edge off Taskin only for the ball to fly through a vacant third slip.
Marnus Labuschagne, on one, wasn't so fortunate.
He poked at an Ebadot ball outside off stump and edged to Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto at second slip, leaving Australia 61-3.
Cameron Green came in and played some big shots before chipping Taskin to short midwicket, where Mushfiqur Rahim took an easy catch.
Wicketkeeper Alex Carey looked in good touch after lunch and cruised to 19 until he played on to Ebadot with the score on 129.
Taskin then produced the ball of the day to beat Beau Webster's bat and clip the top of off stump to leave the home side struggling on 152-6.
Cummins tried to steer the hosts to tea without further loss, however Shanto brought Hasan back into the attack with immediate success, the Australian skipper getting a big edge to Litton.
Hasan got his fourth in the same fashion, Mitchell Starc getting a thin edge to the keeper with the score on 172.
Smith threw his wicket away going for a big hit before Nathan Lyon was last man out in similar fashion.
Bangladesh started their reply confidently and eased to 36 before Australia got the breakthrough, Shadman Islam (20) getting a leading edge off Mitchell Starc to Lyon at backward point.

item.title: Emirates offers Dubai transit visas to Bangladeshi travellers
item.description:
Bangladeshi travellers flying to international destinations can obtain a 96-hour Dubai transit visa through selected Emirates Holidays packages, allowing them to stay in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for up to four days.
According to an Emirates Holidays press release, the facility is particularly useful for passengers travelling from Bangladesh to destinations including the UK, US, Europe, Mauritius, Jordan, Egypt and Türkiye, as well as those travelling for Umrah.
Under the new arrangement, eligible Bangladeshi travellers can apply for the 96-hour transit visa by purchasing designated Emirates Holidays packages that include a four-day stay in Dubai.
The facility will allow travellers to make a short stopover in Dubai during their international journeys, offering them an opportunity to explore one of the world’s leading aviation and tourism hubs.
The transit visa is also expected to make travel more convenient for long-haul passengers using Dubai as a connecting hub.

item.title: Tk 4.38cr missing from Agrani Bank vault in Ctg, 2 held
item.description:
Police have arrested two people, including a senior official of Agrani Bank, in a case filed over the missing of Tk 4.38 crore from the vault of its Laldighi East Corporate branch in Chittagong.
The arrestees are Md Kamrul Hossain, 41, senior officer and cash in-charge of the branch, and Md Jafrullah Tanvir, 25.
They were arrested after the bank authorities filed a case with Kotwali Police Station.
Bank's General Manager Mostak Ahmed filed the case naming Kamrul and Jafrullah as accused along with several unidentified others.
According to the case statement, Kamrul was responsible for the branch's cash and vault. A discrepancy was detected on August 9 while officials were reconciling the cash transactions of the day with the cash kept in the vault after regular banking operations.
Subsequent scrutiny of the accounts, vault records and relevant documents revealed a shortage of Tk 4.38 crore.
The bank alleged that Kamrul, with the assistance of Jafrullah and unidentified others, removed the money from the vault.
Inspector (Investigation) Md Iqbal Hossain of Kotwali Police Station, who is investigating the case, said the two named accused were arrested. A court later sent them to jail, he said.

item.title: CUET declares campus ponds, ditches hazardous after 3 student drownings
item.description:
Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) has declared all campus ponds and ditches hazardous and banned students from bathing or swimming in them following the drowning of three students.
The directive was issued in a notice signed by Professor Saiful Islam, director of the Directorate of Students’ Welfare, on Thursday.
The notice said all campus ponds had been declared hazardous in the interest of students’ safety. Until further notice, entering, swimming or otherwise going into any campus pond is strictly prohibited.
Violators will be considered to have breached university discipline and face disciplinary action under the university’s rules, the notice said.
CUET currently has two ponds and several ditches on its campus. The decision came after three students drowned in one of the ponds in recent weeks.
On Wednesday, second-year students Chomok Dutta of the Computer Science and Engineering Department and Shanto Deb of the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department drowned while bathing in the pond.
Earlier, on July 28, fourth-year Mechanical Engineering student Arnab Saha drowned in the same pond.
According to CUET sources, Shanto and Arnab had entered the pond beside Kazi Nazrul Islam Hall to bathe with friends. They were submerged at one point and later rescued and taken to hospital, where doctors declared them dead.
The latest deaths occurred just two weeks after Arnab’s drowning, leaving the university community in mourning once again.

item.title: Fertilizer sales irregularities grip Rajshahi, farmers protest
item.description:
Farmers across the Rajshahi region are struggling to buy subsidised fertiliser at government-fixed prices, amid allegations of hoarding, diversion and an organised syndicate involving dealers and unauthorised retailers.
The crisis comes as Aman planting is underway, raising concerns among farmers that delays in getting fertiliser could affect crop yields.
Farmers allege that some dealers sell fertiliser allocation orders to black-market traders even before receiving supplies. Others reportedly sell fertiliser directly to retailers from warehouses instead of distributing it through designated outlets. There are also allegations that fertiliser allocated to one district or upazila is being diverted to another.
During visits to several rural areas of Rajshahi, most authorised dealers were found without subsidised fertiliser, while nearby retail shops were selling the same products at significantly higher prices.
Under government-fixed rates, a 50kg bag of triple super phosphate (TSP) costs Tk1,350 and a bag of diammonium phosphate (DAP) Tk1,050. Farmers, however, said they were paying Tk1,700–1,800 for TSP and around Tk1,600 for DAP because of shortages at authorised outlets.
“I have a farmer’s card. I went to authorised dealers several times but could not buy fertiliser,” said Russel Hossain, a farmer from Baraikuri village in Paba upazila.
“Fertiliser is not available at the government-fixed price. But if you are willing to pay more, there is no shortage.”
At M/s Haque & Sons Enterprise, an authorised Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) dealer at Nowhata Bazar in Paba, no subsidised fertiliser was available during the visit.
Dealer Abdul Haque said he supplies fertiliser to several thousand farmers across 42 mouzas.
“In July, I received only 22 bags of TSP, 70 bags of MOP and 110 bags of DAP. The supplies were exhausted within two or three days,” he said.
An employee of Tasnim Enterprise, another authorised dealer, also said the shop’s fertiliser stock had run out. However, shop owner Fazlur Rahman later said fertiliser was available and claimed the employee had provided incorrect information.
At a nearby retail shop, an employee offered to sell a 50kg bag of DAP for Tk1,600, Tk550 above the government-fixed price. He said the shop collected fertiliser from various sources and claimed subsidised fertiliser passed through three or four middlemen before reaching retailers.
Farmers have long alleged that a syndicate involving dishonest dealers, unauthorised retailers and officials responsible for monitoring fertiliser distribution is controlling the market.
Several farmers, speaking on condition of anonymity, alleged that field-level agricultural officials were involved in the network. They also claimed that hundreds of unauthorised fertiliser retailers were operating as part of the system.
Sajedur Rahman, a farmer from Chhoto Palashi village in Rishikul Union of Tanore, said farmers could not find fertiliser at government-fixed prices.
“When we go to the dealers, they say there is no fertiliser. We are forced to buy from high-priced retail shops,” he said.
Farmers in Palashi said TSP was selling for Tk1,700–1,800 per bag, while DAP was available for around Tk1,600. MOP, officially priced at Tk1,050, was reportedly being sold for about Tk500 more.
Despite the allegations, officials said they had not received complaints about a fertiliser shortage.
Azizur Rahman, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Rajshahi division, said, “We have not received any complaints from farmers about a fertiliser shortage. Aman planting is underway everywhere, and agricultural officials are advising farmers.”
Kazi Shahidul Islam, Rajshahi district administrator and chairman of the district fertiliser distribution committee, said he had not received complaints about higher prices but promised to investigate.
According to Agriculture Ministry data, Rajshahi received higher allocations of TSP, DAP and MOP in July and August this year than during the same period in 2025.
The combined allocation rose from 5,876 tonnes in July 2025 to 7,033 tonnes in July 2026. August allocations also increased, with TSP rising from 1,430 tonnes to 1,511 tonnes, DAP from 2,404 tonnes to 2,647 tonnes and MOP from 1,709 tonnes to 1,760 tonnes.
Nasir Uddin, assistant director (fertiliser) at the BADC Rajshahi office, said the agency was distributing fertiliser according to the quantities approved by the Agriculture Ministry. He added that seasonal demand had increased because some farmers were applying fertiliser beyond recommended doses.
The Rajshahi agricultural region, comprising Rajshahi, Natore, Naogaon and Chapainawabganj, has set a target of cultivating Aman rice on 410,000 hectares. About 40% of the targeted area had been planted as of Wednesday.
Meanwhile, farmers in Chapainawabganj’s Gomastapur upazila staged a protest on Wednesday after failing to obtain adequate fertiliser from dealers.
Farmers from Rahonpur Union gathered at the upazila parishad premises and later met Upazila Nirbahi Officer Zillur Rahman.
They said fertiliser was unavailable during a critical stage of Aman cultivation and warned that delays could reduce crop yields.
Gomastapur Upazila Agriculture Officer Saklain Hossain said officials were monitoring the supply situation and would take action if problems were found.
UNO Zillur Rahman said necessary measures were being taken to ensure farmers received fertiliser at government-fixed prices. He warned that legal action would be taken against anyone found selling fertiliser above the fixed price, hoarding supplies to create an artificial shortage, or harassing farmers.

item.title: Hasan’s county lessons pay off with historic six-for in Australia
item.description:
Hasan Mahmud’s historic six-wicket haul in Darwin was not simply the product of a good day with the ball.
The Bangladesh pacer believes the experience he gained playing county cricket in England helped him understand the conditions, trust his judgement and deliver the career-best performance that made him the first Bangladeshi pacer to claim a five-wicket haul on Australian soil.
Hasan returned figures of 6-55 in the first Test against Australia, producing the best bowling figures of his Test career and completing a milestone that had eluded every Bangladesh fast bowler before him. His spell also became the first five-for by a Bangladeshi bowler in Australia across all three formats.
For Hasan, though, the achievement was rooted in lessons learned thousands of kilometres away.
“In terms of experience, I would say that I have found two similar conditions,” Hasan said. “After bowling there, I feel more confident about how to bowl in these conditions or what length to bowl.”
That confidence was evident as Hasan exploited a surface offering moisture, softness and seam movement. Rather than searching for something extraordinary, he and the rest of Bangladesh’s pace attack stuck to a disciplined plan.
“The wicket had a little moisture in the morning, it was soft and there was seam movement. We planned to bowl in disciplined manner and to bowl in partnerships and that is what happened,” he said.
Hasan’s performance was particularly significant because it came against an Australian batting line-up featuring some of the biggest names in Test cricket. His wickets included Travis Head, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Steve Smith and Nathan Lyon, with Smith’s dismissal standing out.
The former Australian captain had made 71 and was attempting to resist Bangladesh’s pressure when Hasan sensed an opportunity to attack him with the short ball.
“I will say Smith’s wicket especially, he was not able to predict. My instinct was working that he would do something, so I hit the bouncer and he missed,” Hasan said.
It was a revealing answer from a bowler who appeared increasingly comfortable trusting his instincts on the biggest stage. Yet Hasan was unwilling to separate his six-for from the work of his fellow pacers.
“Ebadot and Taskin bowled very well from the other end, allowing us to ultimately build that pressure. It ended well for us,” he said.
That collective pressure allowed Hasan to keep returning to the attack and eventually complete the best figures of his Test career. More importantly, it turned a personal milestone into a defining performance for Bangladesh.
Hasan had spoken before the tour about wanting to take at least five wickets in an innings twice in Australia. He needed only one innings to take the first step towards that ambition.
His approach, however, remained refreshingly simple.
“I just bowled according to the line and length, tried to follow the process and follow what the captain said,” he said.
The impact of his spell was amplified by Bangladesh’s response with the bat, as Mominul Haque and Tanzid Hasan built a steady partnership after Shadman Islam’s dismissal.
“The batters also responded well. Unfortunately Shadman Islam was dismissed but Mominul Haque and Tanzid Hasan Tamim built a partnership which edged us ahead,” Hasan said.
For a bowler whose preparation in England had helped him feel more at home in unfamiliar conditions, Australia provided the stage for a historic breakthrough.

item.title: Messi returns but Miami knocked out of Leagues Cup
item.description:
Lionel Messi made an emotional return Wednesday following his father's death and hints at retirement, but it wasn't enough for his Inter Miami side who were knocked out of the Leagues Cup in a 3-2 loss to Mexico's Leon.
The Miami captain flew back to Florida from Argentina on Tuesday night after attending the funeral of his father, Jorge, on Sunday and came on at half-time to a massive ovation.
Jorge, who was his son's agent, died last week at the age of 68.
On Wednesday morning, Messi posted an emotional tribute to his father on social media, admitting that he wasn't sure he wanted to continue playing football.
"I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on," Messi wrote.
"I just played football, and now I have serious doubts about continuing to do so for much longer."
Miami led 1-0 but two goals from Colombian Daniel Arcila fueled Leon's come-from-behind victory, which made them the first team to qualify for the quarter-finals of the tournament between MLS and LigaMx clubs.
Messi had made himself available to Miami coach Guillermo Hoyos for the must-win final group match, having been absent when they lost to Monterrey on Saturday.
Yannick Bright, who scored one of Miami's goals, called Messi's return "incredible," adding he and other teammates just wanted to support their captain.
"I wasn’t expecting it," Bright said. "It shows how much he cares. When I saw he was here, all I was thinking about was to give my 150 percent for him.
"It's a tough situation. We try to stay close to him and support him as much as we can, but it's a lot."
Brazilian teammate Casemiro, who joined Miami after the World Cup, said Messi was "an example for all of us" in his commitment to playing during such a difficult time personally.
Leon coach Javier Gandolfi echoed those thoughts.
"Today he demonstrated once more what he's made of," Gandolfi said of Messi. "He is a human being that is different to the rest."
It is the first time Miami have been knocked out in the opening phase since the Leagues Cup was expanded in 2023.
Miami lifted the trophy that year with Messi, shortly after he arrived at the Florida franchise alongside Spaniards Sergio Busquets and Jordi Alba.
Miami reached the 2025 final but were beaten 3-0 by the Seattle Sounders -- a match marked by a brawl after the final whistle which led to Luis Suarez being suspended for all of this year's tournament.

item.title: City star Doku signs five-year contract extension
item.description:
Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku signed a five-year contract extension with the Premier League club on Thursday.
Doku has developed into one of the most dynamic forwards in the Premier League since joining from French club Rennes in 2023.
The 24-year-old has scored 22 goals and provided 34 assists in 131 games for City, helping the club win the Premier League, the Club World Cup, the FA Cup and the League Cup.
Doku has earned 48 caps for Belgium and featured for his country at the recent World Cup.
Keeping Doku in Manchester until at least 2031 is a major boost for new City boss Enzo Maresca ahead of the Premier League campaign, which starts on August 21.
Maresca has replaced Pep Guardiola at the Etihad Stadium and Doku said the Italian's style of play was instrumental in his decision to commit his long-term future to City.
"I have loved my time at City so far, so to have the opportunity to stay for longer is a fantastic feeling," Doku said.
"This club means so much to me – I have developed as both a player and a person. I feel settled here, and I know I am improving every day because of the work the staff here do.
"With Enzo here now I am really excited about the new season. His style of football is the kind we love, so that's exciting for the players."
City director of football Hugo Viana added: "Jeremy is a huge talent whose improvement since joining us in 2023 is clear for all to see.
"He has a special dynamic. He has the right characteristics for what we are looking for in a winger. He really does bring a special quality to our team.
"He deserves this new deal, and I know he will continue his improvement in the coming months and years."

item.title: ‘I was lucky’: Smith admits technology saved him after DRS scare
item.description:
Steve Smith admitted he believed he had edged Ebadot Hossain and was fortunate to survive after technology overturned Bangladesh’s caught-behind appeal on the opening day of the first Test at Marrara Stadium on Thursday.
Smith was batting on seven in the 21st over when Ebadot delivered full and outside off, drawing the Australian into a tentative poke. The ball went through to wicketkeeper Litton Das and Bangladesh immediately appealed, but umpire Kumar Dharmasena was unmoved.
Bangladesh reviewed the decision, expecting the replay to confirm the edge. Smith, meanwhile, had already begun walking towards the pavilion, seemingly convinced that he had been caught.
But Real Time Snicko showed no clear spike as the ball passed the bat, and the original not-out decision was upheld.
Smith returned to the crease and made Bangladesh pay for the reprieve, eventually top-scoring for Australia with a composed 71 off 109 balls.
“I was lucky? Yeah, it seems that way. You’ve got to take it sometimes,” Smith said after the day’s play.
Asked whether he had actually nicked the ball, the former Australia captain admitted he believed he had.
“I think so, yeah,” he said.
Smith also acknowledged that he had been prepared to walk had he been given out.
“Normally, it’s pretty good. Maybe I didn’t nick it, I don’t know, but I certainly felt something. If I’d been given out, I was going to walk off. But, yeah, technology saved me today, I guess.”
The incident was Smith’s second major escape of the innings.
Earlier, on just two, he edged another delivery from Ebadot towards third slip, where Tanzid Hasan Tamim got both hands to a difficult low chance but could not hold on.
Smith made full use of both reprieves, settling into his innings as Australia struggled against Bangladesh’s disciplined pace attack. He struck seven fours and a six before Hasan Mahmud finally ended his resistance for 71.
Smith advanced down the track to a short delivery outside off and attempted an upper cut, but extra bounce caused him to miscue the shot towards the slip cordon. Litton called for the catch and completed it comfortably.
His dismissal capped a remarkable spell from Hasan, who claimed a career-best six for 55 as Bangladesh bowled Australia out for 198.
Ebadot and Taskin Ahmed claimed two wickets apiece as Bangladesh’s fast bowlers exploited a green surface with early movement and bounce.
Australia’s struggles made Smith’s contribution even more valuable, with Jake Weatherald’s 23 the next-best score in their innings.
Bangladesh then made an assured start in reply, reaching 96 for one by stumps to trail by only 102 runs. Tanzid was unbeaten on 32 and Mominul Haque on 35.
For Smith, the day could easily have ended very differently. Instead, a combination of a dropped catch and technology gave him the opportunity to produce Australia’s highest score — a reprieve he admitted he was fortunate to receive.

From teaching to politics, Mirza Fakhrul set to become President
item.description:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir entered into politics during his student days at the University of Dhaka. He was also jailed for political reasons during the 1969 mass uprising. After independence, he began his professional career as a teacher. He later left teaching to enter politics. Over his long political career, he has served as president of the district BNP, senior joint secretary general, acting secretary general and secretary general of the party. During this time, he rose from municipal chairman to state minister and minister. Now, he is set to become the country’s 23rd president.

The BNP has nominated Mirza Fakhrul for the presidency. As the party has an absolute majority in Parliament, it is almost certain that he will become president. He has already resigned as the party’s secretary general and as a member of its National Standing Committee. If everything goes as planned, he will be elected on 20 August and move to Bangabhaban, the presidential residence.

Professor Manotosh Kumar Dey, a veteran educator from Thakurgaon and a friend of Mirza Fakhrul, expressed his delight at his friend’s nomination.

“My friend will hold the office of president. That is a matter of pride not only for me but also for the people of the country. However, it is painful to think that we, the people of Thakurgaon, will be deprived of his proximity. The development initiatives that have been created in the area under his leadership could lose momentum, and that would be a matter of concern for us,” Manotosh said.

Birth, upbringing and student politics

Born on 26 January, 1948, Mirza Fakhrul grew up in the Kalibari area of Thakurgaon town. His father was Mirza Ruhul Amin and his mother was Mirza Fatema Amin. Mirza Ruhul Amin was elected a member of Parliament from Thakurgaon several times and later served as a minister in the Ershad government. After completing his secondary education at Thakurgaon Government Boys’ High School and higher secondary education at Dhaka College, Mirza Fakhrul earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees in economics from the University of Dhaka.

Mirza Fakhrul entered politics during his student life. He was a member of the then East Pakistan Chhatra Union and was elected general secretary of the organisation’s SM Hall unit at the University of Dhaka. Later, during the 1969 mass uprising, he served as president of the Dhaka University unit. He was also imprisoned for political reasons during this period.

Began career as a teacher

After independence, Mirza Fakhrul began his professional career in 1972 as a lecturer at Dhaka College after joining the BCS Education cadre. Later, during President Ziaur Rahman’s tenure, he served as private secretary to then Deputy Prime Minister SA Bari. After SA Bari resigned in 1982, he returned to teaching. While working at Thakurgaon Government College, he served as deputy director of the government’s Directorate of Inspection and Audit and also worked with the Bangladesh National Commission for UNESCO.

Entering active politics

In 1988, he was elected chairman of Thakurgaon pourashava as an independent candidate. After the anti-autocracy movement of the 1990s, he joined the BNP. He contested the 1991 national election as a BNP candidate. In 1992, he became president of Thakurgaon district BNP. At the same time, he served as a central vice-president of the Krishak Dal.

After being elected a member of Parliament from the Thakurgaon-1 constituency in the 2001 election, he served as state minister for agriculture and later as state minister for civil aviation and tourism in the BNP government.

At the BNP’s fifth national council in 2009, Mirza Fakhrul was elected senior joint secretary general of the party. During the tenure of the then Awami League (whose activities are banned) government, he became widely known in the media as the opposition party’s spokesperson.

Following the death of then BNP Secretary General Khondkar Delwar Hossain in March 2011, party chairperson Khaleda Zia appointed him acting secretary general. At the BNP’s sixth national council on 16 March, 2016, he became secretary general.

After the BNP won the 13th national parliamentary election in 2026 and formed the government, Mirza Fakhrul was given charge of the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives. The party nominated him for the presidency today. He has already resigned as BNP secretary general and as a member of the National Standing Committee.

Besides politics, he has also been involved in sports and cultural activities.

Personal and family life

Mirza Fakhrul is married. His wife, Rahat Ara Begum, works at an insurance company in Dhaka. Their elder daughter, Mirza Shamaruh, studied at the University of Dhaka and later taught there. She currently lives in Australia and is a postdoctoral fellow. Their younger daughter, Mirza Safaruh, studied at the University of Dhaka and currently teaches at a school in Dhaka.

Mirza Fakhrul’s younger brother, Mirza Faisal Amin, is president of Thakurgaon district BNP. His uncle, Mirza Golam Hafiz, was a former land minister and law minister in the BNP government and speaker of the second Parliament. Another uncle, Wing Commander SR Mirza, served in the Mujibnagar government-in-exile in 1971. He was appointed head of the Directorate of Youth Camps, which was established to oversee training facilities for freedom fighters.

Thakurgaon district BNP General Secretary Paygam Ali told Prothom Alo that Mirza Fakhrul Islam has played an important role in national politics for many years. He said they were extremely pleased by the news of his nomination.

“We hope he will serve the country with his experience and wisdom,” he said.

item.title: TUCSAA calls for ensuring good governance in labour migration
item.description:
The Trade Union–Civil Society Action Alliance (TUCSAA) has stressed the need for more effective steps in policy and law implementation, accountability of government institutions, and coordinated efforts from all relevant parties to ensure governance, workers' rights, and protection in the migration sector.

These issues were highlighted today, Thursday at the national conference on Rights-Based Labour Migration Governance and Collective Advocacy held at the Probashi Kalyan Bhaban in Dhaka.

Representatives from trade unions, civil society, government institutions, employer organisations, migrant and returned workers, academics, development partners, and media participated in the conference.

TUCSAA Convener and General Secretary of Bangladesh Labour Federation, Shakil Akhtar Chowdhury, expressed concern at the limited reintegration of a large number of returned migrants each year during the commencement of the event.

In the welcome speech, TUCSAA advisor and Chairman of WARBE Development Foundation, Syed Saiful Haque, said, “We’ve been advocating for a long time through soft and mild-mannered approaches, but continuing this way won't effectively safeguard migrant workers' rights.”

He added that it is not enough to create policies and rules; their implementation must be ensured. A strong and integrated effort is also needed to bring grassroots experiences and issues to the national level.

Razequzzaman Ratan, President of Socialist Labour Front, said, "Migrant workers are sending billions of dollars to the country, but what are they gaining and losing in return?"

He emphasised that considering the contribution of migrant workers to the country's economy, the state should increase its investment in their protection and welfare.

The conference discussed various issues, including high migration costs, irregularities in recruitment, workers' rights violations abroad, limited access to justice, skill gaps, weaknesses in TTCs, human trafficking, irregular migration, and reintegration of returned workers.

Emphasis was placed on bringing grassroots experiences to the national level, proper registration and data preservation of migrant workers, increasing coordination and accountability of government institutions, resolving complexities in recovering unpaid wages based on returning workers' experiences, and the need for easily accessible helplines, emergency assistance, and safe accommodations for female workers.

Additionally, there were calls for policy formulation and implementation with increased participation of migrant workers, trade unions, and civil society, focusing on skill development according to international labour market demands, improvement in training quality and infrastructure, effective reintegration assistance, and specialized training for female workers.

Special guest, ATM Mahbub-ul Karim, Joint Secretary and director, Wage Earners Welfare Board, Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, noted that many workers are going abroad without adequate skills.

He suggested starting counseling and preparation earlier, even from their education life.

He further stated, "From 1 January 2026, data collection of outgoing and returning workers is being implemented, which will help in future planning for sending and reintegration of workers."

The national conference was organised as a continuation of TUCSAA's recent district-level consultative meetings and other activities. The focus was on advancing necessary reforms in the labour migration system by incorporating grassroots experiences and recommendations into national-level discussions.

TUCSAA believes that the success of labour migration cannot be measured only by the number of workers sent abroad and the amount of remittances. It is equally important how safely a worker went abroad, received fair wages and a good work environment, and the support they received upon returning home. This alliance is committed to ensuring that.

TUCSAA Advisor and Executive Director of BILS, Sultan Uddin Ahmed, urged for the immediate preparation of action plans with short- and medium-term plans and said, "To keep this platform running, member organisations must start working self-motivated, sharing responsibilities in networking, research, and fund-raising."

item.title: Severe gas crisis triggers protests, highway blockade in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
Severe gas shortages have caused widespread suffering in Brahmanbaria, disrupting cooking at homes and forcing CNG filling stations to shut down.

The crisis began late Wednesday night in Sarail and spread to several parts of the district from Thursday morning.

The shortage also triggered protests by CNG-run auto-rickshaw drivers, who blocked the Dhaka-Sylhet highway in protest against the closure of filling stations.

Around 1pm today, the drivers blocked the road in front of a CNG station in Kuttapara area of Sarail upazila. The blockade caused long traffic jams on both sides of the highway. They later withdrew following intervention by highway police.

Abdul Halim, inspector (operations) of Sarail Khatihata Highway Police Station, told Prothom Alo that several CNG-run auto-rickshaw drivers, unable to get gas, had gathered on the highway and attempted to create disorder by placing bricks and stones on the road. Police arrived after being informed and dispersed them.

According to local residents, gas supply was cut off without prior notice in parts of Sarail and Sadar upazila late Wednesday night. Gas briefly returned around 3pm Thursday but was cut off again shortly afterwards.

As a result, many households were unable to cook. Some residents cooked on clay stoves, while others bought food from hotels.

Hasna Hena, a lecturer at Brahmanbaria United College and a resident of Pairtala area, said gas supply to her home stopped in the morning.

“I waited until noon, but the gas did not return. With no other option, I bought food from a hotel for lunch,” she told Prothom Alo on Thursday afternoon.

Bashirul Islam, a resident of Kuttapara in Sarail, said such a severe shortage had not occurred recently. “There was no gas in our household stove from morning until 3pm. Supply returned after 4pm but the pressure was low. It stopped again shortly afterwards,” he said.

Upon inquiry, it was learned that residents in various parts of the district have been facing gas cuts every day from 11pm to 6am for about a year.

Gas pressure also remains low at different times during the day. But on Thursday, residents in several areas received virtually no gas throughout the day.

Aklima Begum, a resident of Kandipara in the town, said she could not cook despite waiting all day.

“I could not even turn on the stove since morning. My sons bought bread from a shop and ate it. How are we supposed to manage if there is no gas like this?” she said.

The gas shortage has also affected transport services. CNG-run auto-rickshaw drivers have allegedly been charging passengers higher fares because they cannot obtain gas.

Shankar Das, a resident of Medda area in the town, travelled to Kamoura in Ashuganj for urgent work. He said the fare from Kumarshil intersection to Sarail Bishwaroad is normally Tk50 per person by CNG-run auto-rickshaw, but he had to pay Tk70 on Thursday. “I had to spend an additional Tk 40 for the round trip,” he said.

Auto-rickshaw driver Russel Mia said fares had increased because there was no gas at CNG filling stations.

According to the Brahmanbaria office of gas supplier Bakhrabad Gas Distribution Company Ltd, the district has 23,178 residential customers and 161 commercial customers, including small and cottage industries and restaurants.

Daily gas demand in Brahmanbaria is five to six million cubic feet. On average, 9.5 million cubic feet of gas is supplied daily during winter and 8.5 million cubic feet during summer.

Shafiqul Haque, Deputy General Manager of Bakhrabad Gas Distribution Company Limited in Brahmanbaria, told Prothom Alo that gas supply and pressure have decreased in various areas of the district since Wednesday due to LNG-related issues.

This situation arose because of LNG maintenance work. He stated that he does not know when this problem will end.

item.title: Karoline Leavitt to step down
item.description:
USA-TRUMP/

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who earned a reputation for acid putdowns of journalists, is to step down, President Donald Trump announced Wednesday adding she would remain a senior advisor.

Leavitt, 28, the youngest ever US presidential top spokesperson, has been a fiercely loyal Trump defender, delivering fluent and aggressive performances at often combative press briefings.

"Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides, Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family," Trump said on social media.

"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party."

In May, Leavitt announced the birth of her second child -- a girl named Viviana -- just days after delaying her maternity leave following an alleged assassination attempt on Trump when a gunman tried to storm the White House correspondents dinner.

Her departure, just weeks after returning to the job, comes as Trump faces steadily sinking poll numbers and the Republican Party risks defeat in the November midterm congressional elections.

"I am thankful to the President for entrusting me with the distinct privilege of speaking on his behalf at the White House podium," Leavitt said on social media as her departure was announced.

"I have relished holding the liberal media accountable and ensuring the American people hear the truth about President Trump's successes."

Leavitt wrote that after returning to the White House after the birth of her daughter, "I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve" while devoting the attention needed as press secretary.

Leavitt, is a Trump veteran who served in his press office during his first term that ended in 2021 and then as his spokesperson during his 2024 election campaign.

Leavitt's tenure as press secretary saw a revival of regular briefings that had petered out during the first term, but she presided over sea change on White House interactions with journalists.

In February 2025, she stunned the press corps when she announced that the White House itself -- and not an independent association of correspondents -- would choose which reporters got to cover Trump up close in the Oval Office and on Air Force One.

She also facilitated press credentials from right-wing, pro-Trump media outlets, diluting the presence of traditional news media that tend to ask more challenging questions in the briefing room.

Raised in New Hampshire, where her family ran an ice cream shop, Leavitt sent a letter to her university newspaper in 2017 to protest against the fact that a professor had criticized Trump in class.

After Trump's 2020 election loss, She unsuccessfully ran for a seat in Congress in New Hampshire in 2022 on a pro-Trump, pro-gun ownership platform.

She then won his praise for steely television performances during his 2024 re-election campaign.

She signaled her intent to pursue a political path, stating "our country is facing an existential threat from an increasingly extremist Democrat Party that seeks to destroy everything great about America."

"My fight is entering a new phase, but it is far from over."

item.title: Japan protests Putin's first visit to disputed islands
item.description:
President Vladimir Putin visited Russia's far-eastern Kuril islands for the first time on Thursday, prompting protests by Japan which also claims the territory.

Russian-Japanese relations have long been dogged by the contested islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories and seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.

The Kremlin posted a video of Putin on one of the four main islands, with Russian media saying he visited a fish-processing plant and showing him trying local caviar.

It was the first visit by a Russian president since Dmitry Medvedev in 2010.

"The Northern Territories are an inherent part of Japan's territory, both historically and under international law," Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told reporters.

Putin's visit "offends the sentiments of the Japanese people and is absolutely unacceptable," she said, adding that it "made it more difficult to restore relations in the medium to long term."

Putin travelled to the Kuril Islands after visiting the nearby Russian island of Sakhalin on Wednesday, where Russia's navy was conducting drills.

In Sakhalin, Putin, 73, held a meeting "on ensuring the security of Russia's eastern borders," state media reported.

After the visit to the Kuril Islands, Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi summoned Russian ambassador to Japan Nikolai Nozdrev to lodge a "strong protest" against Putin's surprise move.

Motegi told the ambassador in the meeting that Putin's visit would "have an extremely negative impact on Japan-Russia relations" already complicated by Moscow's offensive on Ukraine, according to the ministry's statement.

Russia's embassy in Japan said the ambassador had said the islands were "an integral part of the Russian Federation," that their "status is not subject to doubt" and that Putin's travel there was not "a matter for discussion with foreign states".

Ties between Japan and Russia have worsened since the full-scale conflict in Ukraine began in 2022.

Japan has joined other G7 countries in sanctioning Russia and giving money and non-lethal defence aid to Kyiv.

Putin on Wednesday called Japan's sanctions "unprovoked".

"Japan has identified Russia as a main source of threats. I would like to point out that we are not threatening Japan... On the contrary it has territorial claims against our country," Putin said.

Russia and China have also moved closer, with their navies and air forces conducting joint exercises in areas around Japan, promoting frequent scrambles by Japanese jets.

North Korea, which this month termed Japan's military build-up a "transformation into a war state", has also sent troops and artillery shells to help Russia's war against Ukraine.

Japan's latest defence white paper issued this month again highlighted growing risks from all three countries.

The New York Times reported in July that Russia had turned Japan into a "den of spies" and a key source of dual-use technology needed for its war in Ukraine.

The Soviet Union took the strategically located volcanic archipelago north of Hokkaido in the final days of World War II, and has maintained a military presence there ever since.

The contested isles are part of the volcanic Kuril archipelago, which runs in a broad arc from Russia's Kamchatka peninsula down to Japan's main northern island Hokkaido.

Their population of about 20,000 Russian citizens lives in a harsh climate, but the islands have mineral deposits including gold and silver, and rich fishing grounds.

After the islands were occupied in 1945, Moscow deported their Japanese population of about 17,000 people.

The islands then acquired strategic importance, providing air and sea bases during the Cold War as the Soviet Union confronted the United States and Japan.

"The Kurils have been fortified with Bastion coastal defence missile systems and SU-35 fighter aircraft. These provide Russia with instruments of control over sea lanes in the region, as well as leverage against Japan's claim to the islands," said Yee Kuang Heng, a professor at the Graduate School of Public Policy at the University of Tokyo.

"Putin's visit may be a reminder of the cards he holds and also his displeasure with Japan's continuing sanctions on Russia," Heng told AFP.

item.title: Iran rejects Trump claims of US control over Hormuz as ‘lies’
item.description:
Iran’s military on Thursday rejected as “lies” remarks by US President Donald Trump claiming control of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the strategic waterway was fully under Iranian control.
“The false claims of the United States that ships are passing through the Strait of Hormuz normally ... are nothing more than lies and fabrications,” said Ebrahim Zolfaghari, the spokesperson for Iran’s central military command, Khatam-al Anbiya.
“The Strait of Hormuz is, as in the past, under the complete management and control of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and no commercial ship or tanker without the permission and supervision of the powerful Iranian armed forces has had and will have the possibility of safe passage through this strait,” he said in a video carried by state television.
Iran has kept control of Hormuz, a vital energy conduit, since the outbreak of the war in the Middle East on February 28, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.
In a Wednesday Truth Social post, Trump claimed that the US “has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!”
“Our Naval Blockade is being called, by everyone, ‘A WALL OF STEEL,’ and there is nothing Iran can do about it,” he added.
On Thursday, the head of Iran’s paramilitary Basij forces under the Revolutionary Guards also said that the strait was under Iranian control.
“Today, you see that the Strait of Hormuz is under the management and control of the Islamic Republic, and our country continues on its path in complete security,” said Hossein Taeb according to state television.
Iran’s top diplomat Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said the US makes miscalculations in regard to the waterway.
“The US has long miscalculated due to intelligence failures. Case in point: The war on Iran. Now, an even bigger miscalculation on the Strait of Hormuz,” he said on X.
Iranian parliamentarian and member of the national security commission Behnam Saeedi said the strait is closed to US and Israeli ships.
“Ships belonging to the Zionist regime will not have the right to pass through the Strait of Hormuz under any circumstances, whether in war or peacetime,” he told state TV, adding that “US military ships will also be barred from passing through the Strait.”
Iran and Oman have been in talks to establish a new route through the strait, but negotiations have not yet been finalized.
Tehran, however, says even if the talks produce a new route, that would not on its own open the waterway unless the US meets Iran’s demands.

item.title: Home has a curfew for many Dhaka tenants
item.description:
It is past 11pm in Dhaka. Roads are quieter, shops are closing and workers are heading home. But for some tenants, reaching their building does not always mean they can get inside.
Across parts of the capital, residential buildings routinely lock main gates at 11pm or midnight, leaving late-returning tenants dependent on caretakers or security guards.
Residents in Banasree, Mirpur, Moghbazar, Mohammadpur, Uttara, Jatrabari and Dhanmondi described waiting outside their own buildings until someone woke up to open the gate.
The practice raises a basic question: where does a landlord’s right to secure a property end, and a tenant’s right to independently access the home they pay for begin?
The issue has become more relevant after Dhaka North City Corporation issued tenant-rights guidelines in January, reportedly including provisions for tenants to receive keys to main gates and rooftops for security and emergency purposes.
Rakib Hossain, a Dhanmondi resident who often returns home close to midnight, said: “Our building gate is closed after 11pm. Every day I have to call the caretaker and wake him up to open the gate. It feels uncomfortable to depend on someone else just to enter my own home. I am not a stranger. I am a tenant of this building.”
He said: “I understand the need for security. But there should be a system where residents can enter without having to wait for someone to open the gate every night.”
For Afreen Rahman of Mohammadpur, the problem once meant waiting outside for around 20 minutes because the caretaker’s phone was switched off.
She said: “The worst part was standing in front of the building where I live and still feeling helpless. It was late at night, and I could not even enter my own home.”
The problem is particularly acute for people working night shifts.
Doctors, nurses, journalists, restaurant employees, delivery riders, security personnel and other shift workers may return well after midnight.
Masum Khandaker, who lives in Moghbazar, said: “My job requires me to work at night. Sometimes I reach home at midnight or even later. But even after finishing work, I have to worry about whether the gate will be locked.”
He said: “Security is important, but why should a security measure become a barrier for the people who actually live here?”
Women also described being questioned about why they returned late.
Monalisa Rahman of Jatrabari said: “It is understandable if they need to know who is entering. But it should not become a situation where I have to justify why I came home late.”
Landlords, however, say locking gates is primarily a security measure.
Mohammad Rafique Chowdhury, a landlord in Mohammadpur, said: “We do not close the gate to cause problems for anyone. We do it for security. Our main concern is to prevent outsiders from entering the building at night. If a tenant returns late, the caretaker opens the gate.”
The arrangement also adds to caretakers’ workloads, while fire-safety officials warn that locked exits can become dangerous during emergencies.
Md Jihad Mia, Senior Station Officer, Pallabi, said: “Residential buildings must keep emergency exits and access routes clear at all times. Locking the main gate at night should not prevent residents from entering or, more importantly, from leaving quickly during a fire or other emergency.”
Advocate Samsun Nahar Rita said: “A landlord can take reasonable steps to ensure building security, but this should not restrict a tenant’s normal access to their rented home. If the gate is locked at night, tenants should have a reliable way to enter without depending entirely on a caretaker.”
A locked gate, therefore, is not necessarily the problem if residents have keys, access cards or another independent entry system.
The problem begins when legitimate residents cannot enter without another person’s assistance.
As Dhaka’s working hours become increasingly diverse, residential practices may also need to change.
For a tenant standing outside a locked gate at 1am, the issue is no longer simply about security.
It is about who gets to decide when they can go home.

item.title: Titumir urges NGOs to bring employees under Universal Pension Scheme
item.description:
Adviser to the Prime Minister on the ministries of Finance and Planning, Prof Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, has called upon local and international NGOs to bring their eligible employees under the Universal Pension Scheme, particularly the "Progoti" scheme, to ensure their long-term financial security.
He made the call while joining a discussion on the Universal Pension Scheme organized by the NGO Affairs Bureau in the capital on Thursday through the Zoom platform as the chief guest.
Representatives of around 250 local and international NGOs registered with the NGO Affairs Bureau attended the discussion.
Officials from the National Pension Authority, Finance Division and local and international NGOs also participated.
Executive Chairman of the National Pension Authority Dr Md Suratuzzaman made a detailed presentation on the structure, objectives and benefits of the Universal Pension Scheme, highlighting the importance of the "Progoti" scheme for people working in the NGO sector.
The Universal Pension Scheme is a state-guaranteed social protection programme aimed at ensuring financial security for citizens in their old age. The "Progoti" scheme has been introduced for people working in the private sector, including private organizations, banks, financial institutions, multinational companies and local and international NGOs.
Under the scheme, subscribers can make regular contributions during their working lives and receive a lifelong monthly pension after retirement.
Speaking as the chief guest, Titumir said wider participation in the Universal Pension Scheme was necessary to ensure the future financial security of people working in the private and NGO sectors.
He urged NGO management authorities to inform their eligible employees about the "Progoti" scheme and take necessary initiatives to bring them under its coverage.
Titumir said the government’s goal was to establish a welfare state where the benefits of development would reach people from all sections and professions of society and no one would be left behind.
Titumir said Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman had placed special emphasis on mass education programmes to spread education among the common people. Subsequently, under the leadership of Begum Khaleda Zia, special importance was attached to the expansion of women’s education and empowerment.
He said active participation of the private and NGO sectors was crucial to implementing the government’s commitment, made in the second chapter of its 2026 election manifesto under the section titled “Inclusive Socio-economic Development and Achieving Sustainable State Capacity,” to establish pension funds for ensuring financial security in old age for people employed in the private sector.
He expressed hope that local and international NGOs would play an effective role in bringing their employees under the "Progoti" scheme.
Representatives of different NGOs raised various queries about the Universal Pension Scheme and took part in an open discussion.
In his concluding remarks, NGO Affairs Bureau Director General (Secretary) Dr Mohammad Zakaria urged all concerned to give due importance to the social and financial security of people working in the NGO sector.
National Pension Authority Member (Administration and Finance) Sheikh Kamrul Hasan, NGO Affairs Bureau Director Dr KM Mamun Uzzaman and Barrister Md Khalilur Rahman Khan also spoke at the programme.
The participating NGO representatives said they gained a detailed understanding of the Universal Pension Scheme and expressed positive interest in bringing employees of their respective organizations under the scheme.

item.title: DMP takes zero-tolerance stance on drugs, snatching
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed has directed police to adopt a zero-tolerance approach to drug-related crimes, take effective measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres, and maintain round-the-clock surveillance in snatching-prone areas.
He gave the directives at the monthly crime review meeting for July 2026, held at the Bangladesh Police Auditorium in Rajarbagh in the capital on Thursday. The DMP commissioner instructed police to strengthen intelligence activities alongside regular drives against drug dealers and others involved in drug-related crimes.
He also directed officials concerned to take necessary measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres within their respective police station areas. “If information about such activities is received, immediate legal action should be taken while maintaining regular surveillance,” he said.
To prevent snatching, Mosleh Uddin instructed the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit and Detective Branch (DB) to maintain round-the-clock field presence in coordination with the Crime Division after identifying snatching-prone areas.
He also ordered stronger intelligence surveillance, patrols and operations in those areas and directed the units concerned to work in coordination to bring the criminals to justice.
The DMP chief further asked the officers-in-charge of the relevant police stations and senior officials of the Crime Division to visit the scene of every crime. He stressed the importance of visiting crime scenes in person, collecting necessary evidence and properly examining the circumstances surrounding incidents to establish the facts and make investigations more effective.
Mosleh Uddin also directed field-level police officials to discharge their duties with the highest professionalism, responsibility and dedication to control crime and ensure the safety of city residents.

item.title: JMB member arrested in Savar sent to court
item.description:
Police sent an alleged member of banned militant outfit JMB to court on Thursday, seeking a 10-day remand in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act.
The accused, identified as Mohammad Arif, 26, was arrested by members of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit from Hemayetpur in Savar on Tuesday. He was produced before the court from Savar Model Police Station around noon on Thursday.
According to police, several bombs were recovered from a bag in Arif’s possession at the time of his arrest. Later, based on information provided by him, police raided his rented residence in South Shyampur, Hemayetpur.
During the raid, police recovered several powerful bombs, cocktails and a large quantity of materials allegedly used to make explosives.
Police subsequently filed a case at Savar Model Police Station under the Anti-Terrorism Act, naming six people, including Arif, and several unidentified others as accused.
According to the case statement, the accused are members of the banned New JMB and had gathered in the Savar area with explosives to carry out acts of sabotage.
The statement also alleged that they supported the ideology of the banned organisation and were involved in activities aimed at creating public panic, threatening public safety and national sovereignty, and attempting to attack law enforcement personnel.
The other named accused are currently absconding, police said.
Savar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Saiful Alam said Arif was sent to court with a 10-day remand plea.

item.title: Fakhrul’s presidential nomination sparks celebrations in Thakurgaon
item.description:
Thakurgaon, the birthplace of BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, erupted in celebration after reports that he had been finalized as the party’s candidate for Bangladesh’s 23rd presidential election.
Following a high-level BNP meeting on Thursday, news of Fakhrul’s nomination quickly spread across the district. Party activists and local residents gathered at the BNP office and his ancestral home in Kalibari. Supporters organized celebratory processions, distributed sweets and exchanged greetings, turning parts of the town into a festive scene.
Fakhrul became involved in politics as a student at Dhaka University. He later worked as a college teacher before entering local politics and being elected chairman of Thakurgaon Municipality. He subsequently served as a member of parliament, state minister and full minister.
Over more than a decade of political turbulence, Fakhrul played a significant role in keeping the BNP organized and united. His political career also included periods of imprisonment amid the party’s prolonged political struggles.
Residents described his nomination as a major achievement not only for Thakurgaon but also for the wider northern region.
Prof Abu Bakar Siddique, former principal of Thakurgaon Government Women’s College, described Fakhrul as one of the region’s most distinguished figures. He expressed hope that development initiatives for Thakurgaon would receive greater momentum if Fakhrul assumes the presidency.
Dr ABM Khairul Kabir, president of the Thakurgaon chapter of the Bangladesh Medical Association and a former director of Dinajpur Medical College Hospital, said Fakhrul’s achievement was a source of pride for the entire northern region.
District BNP President Mirza Faisal Amin said the family was deeply moved, calling the nomination recognition of Fakhrul’s lifelong sacrifice, dedication and integrity.
Residents expressed hope that, if elected president, Fakhrul would strengthen democratic institutions and help reflect the hopes and aspirations of ordinary citizens.

item.title: Barbie sequel hangs in the balance as deal talks stall
item.description:
The future of a sequel to 2023’s blockbuster Barbie has been thrown into uncertainty as Warner Bros. and the film’s key creative team remain at odds over new contracts.
The stalled talks involve director and co-writer Greta Gerwig, co-writer Noah Baumbach, star and producer Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling, who played Ken. Warner Bros. has reportedly made more than 6 offers over the past 3 years, with the latest described by a studio source as the biggest offer the company has made to a filmmaking team and its stars.
The team has not accepted the latest proposal, with sources indicating that compensation remains a major sticking point, particularly back-end participation. The negotiations are being handled by CAA, which represents all 4 creatives, with agency chief Bryan Lourd leading the process. Gerwig’s lawyer Tara Kole is also involved.
The dispute comes at a crucial moment for Warner Bros. The studio has roughly 4 months to put a new Barbie film into active development before the rights to the iconic Mattel doll revert to the toymaker.
Gerwig and Baumbach are understood to have an idea for a sequel, but sources say they are unwilling to move forward before agreements are signed.
The original Barbie deals did not include obligations for a sequel. Those agreements were negotiated under a previous Warner regime, and Gerwig reportedly did not want to commit to another film at the time. The studio also had limited reason to anticipate the scale of the film’s eventual success.
That success changed everything. Directed by Gerwig, Barbie became the highest-grossing film in Warner Bros. history, earning more than $1.4 billion worldwide and turning its cast and creative team into some of Hollywood’s most sought-after names.
The new negotiations reportedly include higher upfront fees and increased back-end participation. Gosling is said to be seeking $20 million to reprise his Oscar-nominated role as Ken, while Robbie earned an estimated $50 million in salary and back-end compensation from the first film, with her final earnings expected to be higher.
Gerwig also earned tens of millions of dollars from the original film, making the financial expectations for a follow-up considerably higher.
Sources disagree over the precise terms of the latest offer, but the creative team is reportedly not seeking first-dollar gross, which would allow them to receive box-office payments before the studio recoups its investment.
The impasse has also created uncertainty for Mattel, whose fledgling film and television division scored an early success with Barbie. The company has a deal in place with Warner Bros. but needs the original creative team on board to continue the franchise in its current form.
The stakes extend beyond Hollywood. Barbie doll sales surged around the release of the film in 2023 but have since declined, while Mattel has announced plans to reposition the doll as a fashion icon with an expanded focus on clothing and accessories.
Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav has faced criticism from some industry figures over the negotiations, particularly as the company navigates a potential acquisition by Paramount.
There could, however, be another path forward. If David Ellison succeeds in his bid for Warner Bros., one source suggested he could revive the Mattel rights and bring Gerwig and the rest of the creative team back into the fold.
Representatives for the filmmakers, stars, Warner Bros., Mattel and CAA declined to comment.

item.title: Bihan brings women’s everyday leadership struggles to the screen
item.description:
The everyday barriers that can hold women back from leadership take centre stage in Bihan (The Beginning), a new fiction film produced by Oxfam in Bangladesh as part of its Rise & Lead initiative.
Directed by Hemanta Sadeeq, the film stars Dilruba Doyel and Nishat Priom as Shiuli and Rakhi, 2 working women navigating expectations around behaviour, care responsibilities, confidence and power.
BoxOffice produced the film, with cinematography by Sahil Rony and Hridoy Sarkar. Dhaka Tribune is the media partner of the film.
Rather than relying on dramatic transformations, Bihan explores how social conditioning, workplace realities, family responsibilities and self-doubt can shape women’s professional choices. At the heart of the story is the process through which both women begin to recognise their own agency, voice and potential to lead.
“We intentionally moved away from framing empowerment through grand speeches or dramatic cinematic turns,” director Hemanta Sadeeq said. “The power of Bihan lies in its focus on everyday, subtle friction — because that is precisely where the real barriers to leadership exist. I believe authentic leadership doesn’t always demand an extraordinary catalyst; often, it begins with the quiet realization of one’s own voice.”
The film’s visual language follows the same understated approach, using naturalistic performances and familiar middle-class urban settings to reflect gradual changes in behaviour. Mirrors and reflections recur as motifs of self-discovery, while the final image of a green traffic signal points to movement, possibility and a new beginning.
Nishat Priom said the story appealed to her because of how recognisable its characters are.
“What attracted me to the story is how recognizable these women are. They are capable and responsible, yet they are constantly negotiating expectations at work, at home and within themselves,” she said. “Bihan is about that moment when a woman begins to see her own strength differently. I encourage everyone to watch the film.”
The film is the latest public-facing element of Rise & Lead, Oxfam’s initiative to advance women’s leadership by addressing barriers at individual, community, workplace and structural levels.
“Women’s leadership cannot depend only on asking women to become more confident or ambitious. Institutions, workplaces and families must also change,” said Mahmuda Sultana, Programme Director, Oxfam in Bangladesh. “We need systems that recognize women’s capabilities, redistribute care responsibilities, create fair opportunities and, most importantly, are prepared to share decision-making power.”
Through the story of Shiuli and Rakhi, Bihan translates the initiative’s advocacy agenda into an accessible human narrative, connecting women’s leadership with everyday realities at home, at work and within institutions.
The film has been developed under the supervision of Md Sariful Islam, with Shawon Koiri as writer. The cast also includes Bappy Ashraf, Nazmul Hasan, Aadnan Chowdhury, Prionmoyi Prio and Sayan Rahman.
Bihan will be released on Oxfam in Bangladesh’s social media platforms on August 14 at 8pm.
